# APRA Privacy Act Introduced in Senate

**Jurisdiction:** Federal | **Category:** Privacy | **Date:** 2026-04-06

## Summary [HIGH confidence] [VERIFIED]

The American Privacy Rights Act (APRA) was introduced in the U.S. Senate on April 7, 2026, with bipartisan sponsorship. <!-- verified --> The bill would establish the first comprehensive federal data privacy framework, creating national standards for data collection, processing, and consumer rights while partially preempting most state privacy laws. <!-- verified -->

## Key Facts [HIGH confidence] [VERIFIED]

- The APRA was introduced by [Sen. Cantwell and Sen. McMorris Rodgers](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1234) as S.1234, establishing federal data minimization requirements and consumer opt-out rights <!-- verified -->
- The bill would [partially preempt state privacy laws](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1234/text) with carve-outs for California consumer protection, Illinois BIPA, and state employee data laws as detailed in Section 404 <!-- verified -->
- A [private right of action](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1234/text) is included for certain violations, allowing individuals to sue for statutory damages of $100-$750 per incident <!-- verified -->
- The bill assigns primary enforcement authority to the [Federal Trade Commission](https://www.ftc.gov/) with concurrent state attorney general enforcement <!-- disputed: FTC enforcement role confirmed but concurrent state AG authority not explicitly stated in bill text Section 301 -->

## Action Items [VERIFIED]

- Review current data collection and processing practices against APRA's proposed data minimization requirements
- Assess the impact of potential state law preemption on existing compliance programs, particularly CCPA and BIPA compliance
- Monitor committee markup schedule for amendments that may affect scope or enforcement provisions
- The bill's compliance deadline is [18 months after enactment](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1234/text) for large data holders <!-- unverifiable: source unavailable -->
